transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in today?

Yeah, thanks for seeing me. Well, what really brought me in is that my mind just won't stay on one thing anymore. Like, I'll be sitting at the bench, right? And I'll jump from checking a customer email to looking at a saw mark on the metal... which, honestly, I shouldn't even be getting saw marks right now because I just bought these brand new Swiss jeweler's blades. They're supposed to be top of the line, size 4/0, you know, for really fine detail work. My buddy Dave recommended them—he works over at this shop downtown that mostly does custom engagement rings, really high-end stuff. 

Anyway, I'll be looking at the saw mark, and then I hear a noise outside, like a delivery truck backing up or something, and I'll go look at that, and suddenly I realize I've completely lost the whole work order. Just totally misplaced the paper. It's really frustrating because Dave never loses his work orders, he's got this whole color-coded system going on... but yeah, I just can't keep my focus on what's right in front of me.
Has this trouble focusing been something you've dealt with since childhood, or is this a new change from how your mind used to work?

I don't really know if it's been since I was a kid... I mean, I guess I was okay in school? I don't really remember it being this bad. I did take this metal shop class in high school, though, which is actually how I got into all the metalworking and jewelry in the first place. Mr. Henderson was the teacher, and he had this crazy old lathe in the back of the room. 

It was from like, the 1950s, heavy cast iron, painted this weird seafoam green color that you just don't see on machinery anymore. He used to tell us stories about how they built things to last back then, not like the cheap plastic stuff today. I actually tried to buy a vintage lathe just like that off Craigslist a few months ago, but the guy wanted way too much for it, and the freight shipping would have been an absolute nightmare because it weighs like four hundred pounds. Plus, my apartment is on the second floor, so getting it up the stairs would have been impossible without a winch or something... but yeah, I'm not really sure about when the focus stuff started.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed your mood feeling unusually elevated, euphoric, or irritable, along with having much more energy than usual or needing less sleep?

Yeah, I mean... a little bit of both, I guess? Like, I did this jewelry show recently. It was one of those weekend artisan markets, and I actually had to build my own display cases for it out of this reclaimed barn wood. Which, by the way, is a total nightmare to work with because it's always warped, so you have to plane it down forever, and the sawdust gets absolutely everywhere. I really need a new dust collection system for my shop, honestly, because the one I have right now is basically just a glorified shop vac and it's super loud... 

But anyway, after that show, I just felt completely lit up. Like, larger than life, just this huge rush. But then the next minute, I'd be snapping at literally anyone who asked me to stick to normal shop hours or told me to slow down. Like the guy who leases the studio space next to mine, he's always complaining if I'm running the polishing wheel late. He wears these ridiculous neon yellow suspenders—like, who wears neon yellow suspenders unless you're directing traffic? It's so distracting. But yeah, I just couldn't handle anyone telling me to slow down or stop working, I'd just bite their head off.

How long did that 'lit up,' high-energy, irritable feeling last after the show—was it just that day, or did it continue for several days in a row where you felt noticeably different from your usual self?

It wasn't just that day, no. It started right after they announced I won this award at the show—Best Emerging Artist, which was crazy because the guy who won second place had this massive booth with all these custom glass display cases that he probably paid thousands for. I actually looked into buying those same cases online, but the shipping alone was more than my rent. Plus, the glass is tempered, so if it shatters, it breaks into a million little cubes instead of shards, which is great for safety, but trying to clean that up out of a carpet would be impossible. Not that I have carpet in my shop, it's all concrete, but still. 

But yeah, that wired, totally out-of-control stretch lasted for about two weeks straight. I just couldn't turn it off. I was working on this silver cuff bracelet during that time, trying to do this really intricate chasing and repoussé work, which takes forever because you have to heat the pitch to just the right temperature so it's soft enough to move the metal but not so soft that it sticks to your tools. I actually burned my thumb pretty bad because my torch was acting up—I think the regulator on the acetylene tank is going bad, I need to take it down to the welding supply place on 4th Street to get it checked. The guy who runs it is always super grumpy, though, he acts like you're bothering him just by walking in the door... but anyway, yeah, about two weeks of just feeling completely wired.
Aside from this high-energy period, have you ever had a stretch of at least two weeks where you felt persistently down, empty, or lost interest in things you normally enjoy?

Yeah, actually... right now, really. These past couple weeks have been awful. I just wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling in my chest. It's like... I don't know, like the shine has just completely gone out of everything. I've even sat in my truck and just cried before going in to open the shop. Which is weird because my truck is usually my favorite place to be. It's an '04 Tacoma, manual transmission, which you can't even find anymore. Everyone wants an automatic now, but I like feeling connected to the engine, you know? Though the clutch has been slipping a little in second gear, and I know I need to replace it, but dropping the transmission on a four-wheel drive is such a massive pain. You have to take out the transfer case and everything, and last time I did it, I lost one of the bell housing bolts and had to drive to three different hardware stores to find a replacement with the right thread pitch... but yeah, I just feel totally empty lately.
How many days in a row have you been feeling this down, empty, or hollow—has it been every day for at least two weeks now?

Yeah, it's been every day... probably for about a month now, honestly. Just this heavy, depressed, guilty feeling hanging over me constantly. I haven't even been able to bring myself to look at the new batch of turquoise cabochons I ordered. They're from the Kingman mine, which is supposed to be this really stable, beautiful blue, but honestly, half the time when you order online, they send you stabilized stones that look like plastic. They pump them full of resin so they don't crack when you set them, which I get, but it totally ruins the natural matrix. I prefer working with natural stones, even if they're more fragile. You just have to be super careful when you're pushing the bezel over, otherwise you'll chip the edge, and then the whole piece is ruined and you have to start over. I have this special agate burnisher I use for the final polish on the silver, it's supposed to be gentler, but... yeah, it's been about a solid month of just feeling completely down.
During those two weeks after the show when you felt 'wired' and irritable, did you notice you needed much less sleep than usual—like only a few hours—without feeling tired the next day?

Yeah, that's exactly what happened. I was sleeping maybe two, three hours a night, tops. I'd wake up at like 3 AM, totally clear-headed and just buzzing, you know? I was so excited to start cutting stones or posting new designs online before the sun even came up. I was working on this one piece, a pendant with this crazy piece of Royston ribbon turquoise, which is so hard to find with a good contrast between the brown host rock and the blue vein. You have to be so careful cutting ribbon turquoise because the host rock is softer than the turquoise itself, so if you're not paying attention on the cabbing machine, you'll undercut the edges and it won't sit flat in the bezel. I use a 280-grit diamond wheel for the initial shaping, which is aggressive but gets the job done fast, though it throws water everywhere. I actually need to replace the splash guard on my machine, I've just been using a piece of cardboard taped to the side, which gets soggy after about ten minutes. But yeah, I wasn't tired at all the next day, just ready to keep going.

During those two 'wired' weeks after the show, did you experience anything like hearing voices or sounds others couldn't hear, or believing things—like that you had special powers, a special mission, or that people were plotting against you—that turned out not to be true?

No, no, nothing like that. I didn't hear voices or think I had superpowers or anything. I just felt really, really good, you know? Like I could finally get everything done. Which is a big deal, because my workshop is a total disaster right now. I've been meaning to build this new workbench, a heavy-duty one with a solid maple top. The problem with my current bench is that it wobbles when I'm hammering, and if you're trying to stamp a design into silver and the table gives even a millimeter, you get a double impression and it ruins the whole piece. I was looking at this butcher block countertop at the hardware store, but it's like two inches thick and weighs a ton. I'd have to get my buddy Dave to help me move it, but Dave has been super flaky lately ever since he got that new job at the brewery. He's always talking about hops and fermentation temperatures now, which is cool and all, but he never has time to just hang out. We used to go fishing down at the lake on weekends, but I haven't even had my poles out of the garage since last summer. The line on my favorite reel is probably totally brittle by now. I should really strip it and respool it with braided line, it casts so much smoother... but yeah, no, no voices or anything crazy like that. Just felt really productive.

During this past month of feeling down, have you experienced anything like hearing voices, seeing things others don't see, or having beliefs—such as feeling especially guilty, worthless, or convinced something bad will happen—that others tell you aren't true or seem out of proportion?

No, I haven't heard any voices or seen things that aren't there. But the guilt... yeah. It's just this constant, heavy feeling. I keep replaying every client promise I messed up, every deadline I missed when I was supposedly so "productive." I just keep telling myself I'm a complete fraud. I won that one award at the jewelry show, and now I feel like I've just embarrassed my family because I can't even get out of bed to finish a basic sizing job. Sizing rings is actually the worst part of the job, honestly. People think you just stretch it, but if it's got stones in it, stretching it will pop the seats right out. You have to cut the shank, add a piece of silver, solder it, file it, and then polish it back so you can't see the seam. And if it's a sterling silver ring, silver transfers heat so fast that if you're not careful, you'll melt the whole thing or fry the stone. You have to bury the stone in wet sand or use this special heat-shield paste, which smells terrible when it burns. It gets everywhere, under your fingernails... I can't stand the smell of it. But yeah, I just feel like a total failure, like I'm letting everyone down over this stupid award.

You have to be so careful cutting ribbon turquoise because the host rock is softer than the turquoise itself, so if you're not paying attention on the cabbing machine, you'll undercut the edges and it won't sit flat in the bezel. I use a 280-grit diamond wheel for the initial shaping, which is aggressive but gets the job done fast, though it throws water everywhere. I actually need to replace the splash guard on my machine, I've just been using a piece of cardboard taped to the side, which gets soggy after about ten minutes. But yeah, I wasn't tired at all the next day, just ready to keep going.

Need to clarify if psychotic features were present during mania to differentiate F31.1 vs F31.2, and confirm no substance/medical cause.

patient.answer: No, no, nothing like that. I didn't hear voices or think I had superpowers or anything. I just felt really, really good, you know? Like I could finally get everything done. Which is a big deal, because my workshop is a total disaster right now. I've been meaning to build this new workbench, a heavy-duty one with a solid maple top. The problem with my current bench is that it wobbles when I'm hammering, and if you're trying to stamp a design into silver and the table gives even a millimeter, you get a double impression and it ruins the whole piece. I was looking at this butcher block countertop at the hardware store, but it's like two inches thick and weighs a ton. I'd have to get my buddy Dave to help me move it, but Dave has been super flaky lately ever since he got that new job at the brewery. patient.answer: No, I haven't heard any voices or seen things that aren't there. But the guilt... yeah. It's just this constant, heavy feeling. I keep replaying every client promise I messed up, every deadline I missed when I was supposedly so "productive." I just keep telling myself I'm a complete fraud. I won that one award at the jewelry show, and now I feel like I've just embarrassed my family because I can't even get out of bed to finish a basic sizing job. Sizing rings is actually the worst part of the job, honestly. People think you just stretch it, but if it's got stones in it, stretching it will pop the seats right out. You have to cut the shank, add a piece of silver, solder it, file it, and then polish it back so you can't see the seam. And if it's a sterling silver ring, silver transfers heat so fast that if you're not careful, you'll melt the whole thing or fry the stone. You have to bury the stone in wet sand or use this special heat-shield paste, which smells terrible when it burns. It gets everywhere, under your fingernails... I can't stand the smell of it. But yeah, I just feel like a total failure, like I'm letting everyone down over this stupid award.
